rows.evidence: Q1: Results and discussion, Figs. 3-7 - the authors built an ESP32/DHT22/soil-moisture/water-level prototype and report their own sensor readings recorded on 2 May 2024 (e.g. temperature 22.1-28 C, soil moisture 62.5-65 %) displayed via an SSE web dashboard.
rows.notes: The study concerns a ground-based IoT sensor and web-dashboard irrigation prototype, not remote sensing (no satellite, UAV or imagery data). Even for its own technology it reports only sensor readings and dashboard screenshots; it does not measure water applied, water saved, or compare against conventional irrigation, so there is no result on water conservation. Claims of 'significant improvement in irrigation efficiency' are asserted, not measured.

rows.evidence: Q1: Results and discussion, Figs. 3-7 - own prototype deployment with ESP32 and sensors; one day of sensor data (2 May 2024) and terminal/web/mobile dashboard outputs are reported.
rows.notes: The technology matches (IoT smart-sensor irrigation control with threshold-based pump activation at 38 % soil moisture and a web interface), but the study reports no result on water conservation: no water-use measurement, no comparison with a baseline, no yield or efficiency data. What it shows is that the system can monitor temperature, humidity, soil moisture and tank level in real time and push them to a browser every 20 s. This is a precondition (monitoring/control capability) for the claimed water-saving effect, hence upstream. The authors do list limitations (connectivity, sensor reliability, power, prototype scale, farmer adoption), but these concern the system, not a measured water-conservation result, so Q8 stays 'no' given Q2 is 'no'.

rows.evidence: Q1: Results and discussion, Figs. 3 and 4 - own sensor data from the prototype on 2 May 2024: T 22.1-28 C, RH 39-49.1 %, soil moisture 62.5-65 %, water level 60-62 %.
rows.notes: The ranges quoted in the passage are correctly taken from the study's Figs. 3-4, but they are monitoring readings only. The study does not report any measurement of water consumption or its reduction, nor any irrigation events, pump run-times or comparison with a non-smart baseline; it describes the test as a 'realistic simulation of agricultural conditions' on a prototype over one day. The passage's assertion that this 'validates ... consumption reduction under real operational conditions' is not supported by any reported result. The study only establishes real-time monitoring/control capability, a precondition of water conservation (upstream). The authors themselves note the prototype results may not transfer to larger farms and that reliable connectivity and power are needed, but these are not limitations of a water-saving result because none is reported.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a hardware/software prototype demonstration (ESP32, DHT22, soil moisture and ultrasonic water-level sensors, SSE web dashboard) with one day of sensor readings. No agronomic or water-use outcomes are measured; statements about improved irrigation efficiency, yield stability and water savings are assertions without supporting data.
